topics.topic: CLI entry point and command routing
topics.rationale: The `web` command needs to be added to the CLI parser. The existing `parseArgs` function in `cli.ts` handles `run`, `init`, `help`, `version` — a new `web` command must be added with `--host` and `--port` flags. The `main()` dispatch also needs a new `webCommand` entry point.

The webapp must load and interact with workflows dynamically. The `WorkflowModule` interface (specifically `run()` and optionally `name`/`description`) defines the contract. `loadWorkflow()` and `listWorkflows()` in `workflow-loader.ts` are the discovery mechanism. The web server will need to load workflows and provide them context (via `WorkflowRunOptions`).

The webapp needs access to live phase/agent/task state. `WorkflowStatusTracker` in `workflow-status.ts` tracks current phase, completed phases, tasks, scouting reports, plan, stats. `TaskTracker` in `task-status.ts` manages task DAG state. `AuditLog` captures agent events. These will be the data sources for the frontend's sidebar and main content.

topics.topic: Agent session lifecycle and event callbacks
topics.rationale: The webapp must stream agent activity (turns, messages, thinking, tool calls) to the frontend in real time. The `StatusCallbacks` type and `AgentStatusCallbacks` in `types.ts` define the event hooks. The `createHarness()` function in `harness-factory.ts` wires up these callbacks via `session.subscribe()`. The `TurnContentBlock` type models the message content (text, thinking, toolCall).

No existing web server code exists. A new HTTP server must be built (likely using Bun's built-in `Bun.serve()` or adding a framework like Hono). It needs to: serve the React frontend statically, provide REST/SSE endpoints for workflow state and events, and host the `engin web --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3619` command. This will be a new module, probably `src/web/` or `src/server/`.

A React frontend (dark-mode, CSS variables, sidebar, progress indicators) must be created. There is no existing frontend tooling. The build pipeline (likely using Bun or Vite) needs to produce static assets that the server can serve. Key frontend concerns: CSS variable theme system, virtualized agent log windows, grid layout with minimum column widths, phase progress indicator, sidebar with workflow-defined titles and status indicators.

The develop workflow needs a custom React renderer as described: phase progress indicator at top, agent windows in a responsive grid (minimum column width, rows stretch to fill), virtualized session log scrolled to bottom, initialization phase that calls pi for a title. This renderer will be part of the develop workflow's `main.ts` or a separate frontend module within the workflow directory.

topics.topic: Singleton server pattern and concurrent access
topics.rationale: The webapp should host a singleton server that can handle multiple workflow runs simultaneously. The sidebar shows current and past runs. This requires a registry/manager for active workflow sessions, thread-safe state access, and clean separation between workflow execution and web serving. The `LanePool` in `pool/lane-pool.ts` shows the existing concurrency model.

Adding web serving, React, and frontend tooling will require new npm dependencies. The current `package.json` uses `bun` as runtime, has no React or web framework deps. The `tsconfig.json` has strict settings. Understanding existing conventions for imports, exports, and module resolution is critical for consistency.

reasoning: The codebase (`@harms-haus/engin`) is a Bun-based TypeScript CLI tool for orchestrating multi-agent AI development workflows. It has no existing web server or frontend infrastructure — this is a greenfield addition. The scouting reports provide comprehensive coverage of all existing code: CLI argument parsing (hand-rolled, command dispatch for 'run'/'init'/'help'/'version'), the central type system (StatusCallbacks, WorkflowState, Task, AuditEvent, WorkflowModule, WorkflowRunOptions, WorkflowPhase with 7 phases), config directory resolution (local `.engin/` overrides global `~/.config/engin/`), workflow discovery and dynamic loading (`loadWorkflow()`, `listWorkflows()`), state management (WorkflowStatusTracker persists to `.engin-state.json`, TaskTracker manages DAG task lifecycle with cycle detection, AuditLog records events as JSONL), the two-tier callback architecture (WorkflowStatusCallbacks with 13 hooks + AgentStatusCallbacks with 4 hooks, composed into StatusCallbacks intersection, wired through harness-factory subscriptions and LanePool propagation), and the concurrency model (LanePool with async lanes, AbortController-based cooperative cancellation, exponential backoff, try/finally disposal). The `.engin/work/develop/.engin-state.json` file provides a concrete example of persisted workflow state (currently at scouting_review phase, with completed scouting phase, no tasks, and scoutingReports containing markdown-fenced JSON). No workflow `main.ts` files exist yet. The develop workflow's runtime behavior is described in the task but not yet implemented. The build pipeline uses `tsc` only, ESM with `.js` extension imports, no bundler. Existing dependencies: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, zod, dotenv, gray-matter. No web/frontend dependencies exist. Bun's built-in `Bun.serve()` is available as a zero-dependency HTTP server option.

tasks.title: Create WebSocket bridge from StatusCallbacks to broadcast messages
tasks.prompt:
Create src/web/bridge.ts that bridges StatusCallbacks events into WebSocket broadcasts.

Import types from ./types.js (ServerMessage, LogEntry, AgentWindowState) and from ../core/types.js (StatusCallbacks, TurnContentBlock).

Define and export a type BroadcastFn = (message: ServerMessage) => void.

Export a function createWebCallbacks(runId: string, broadcast: BroadcastFn): StatusCallbacks that returns a full StatusCallbacks object. Each callback translates its event into the appropriate ServerMessage and calls broadcast(). Implementation for each:

- onWorkflowStart: No-op.
- onPhaseStart: Broadcast { type: 'workflow_phase', workflowId: runId, phase: info.phase, completed: [] }.
- onPhaseComplete: Broadcast { type: 'workflow_phase', workflowId: runId, phase: info.phase, completed: [info.phase] }.
- onAgentSpawn: Broadcast { type: 'agent_spawned', workflowId: runId, agent: { agentId: info.agentId, profile: info.profile, taskId: info.taskId, active: true, log: [] } }.
- onAgentComplete: Broadcast { type: 'agent_complete', workflowId: runId, agentId: info.agentId }.
- onTurnEnd: For each contentBlock in info.contentBlocks, create a LogEntry with id=crypto.randomUUID(), timestamp=new Date().toISOString(). Map block types: text -> { type:'text', content: block.text }; thinking -> { type:'thinking', content: block.thinking, metadata: { redacted: block.redacted } }; toolCall -> { type:'text', content: formatted string showing tool name and args summary }. Broadcast { type: 'agent_log', workflowId: runId, agentId: info.agentId, entry }.
- onToolCallStart: Create LogEntry with type 'tool_call_start', content=info.toolName, metadata with toolCallId. Broadcast agent_log.
- onToolCallEnd: Create LogEntry with type 'tool_call_end', content=info.toolName, metadata with isError. Broadcast agent_log.
- onDecision: Create LogEntry with type 'decision', content=info.decision. Broadcast agent_log.
- onError: Create LogEntry with type 'error', content=info.error. Broadcast agent_log.
- onWorkflowComplete: Broadcast { type: 'workflow_complete', workflowId: runId, durationMs: info.totalDurationMs }.
- onWorkflowFailed: Broadcast { type: 'workflow_failed', workflowId: runId, error: info.error.message, phase: info.phase }.
- onSidebarUpdate: Broadcast { type: 'workflow_sidebar', workflowId: runId, sidebar: { title: info.title ?? '', indicator: info.indicator ?? '' } }.
- onTurnStart, onTaskStart, onTaskComplete, onTaskRejected: No-op.

Each callback should be wrapped in a try/catch that logs errors to console.error so broadcast failures do not crash the workflow.

tasks.title: Create Bun.serve HTTP and WebSocket server
tasks.prompt:
Create src/web/server.ts that starts the engin web server using Bun.serve().

Import from node:path and node:fs. Import types from ./types.js. Import WorkflowRunRegistry from ./registry.js. Import createWebCallbacks from ./bridge.js. Import loadWorkflow from ../core/workflow-loader.js. Import getDefaultWorkDir from ../core/config.js.

Export an async function startWebServer(options: WebServerOptions): Promise<void>.

Implementation:

1. Create a registry instance: new WorkflowRunRegistry(options.cwd).

2. Maintain a Set of connected WebSocket clients. Use Bun.serve with a websocket property to manage them.

3. Define a broadcast function that iterates all clients and calls client.send(JSON.stringify(message)). Skip clients that are not open.

4. The Bun.serve call should configure:

   fetch(req, server): Response | undefined:
   - Parse the URL from req.
   - GET /api/workflows: Return Response.json(registry.getAllRuns()).
   - GET /api/workflows/:id: Extract id from URL pathname. Look up agents from registry. Return Response.json with summary and agents. Return 404 if not found.
   - POST /api/workflows: Read body as JSON. Validate workflowName and taskPrompt are present. Call startWorkflow (inner function). Return Response.json({ id: runId }, { status: 201 }).
   - GET /ws: Call server.upgrade(req) and return undefined to upgrade to WebSocket.
   - All other GET requests: Serve static files from the frontend build directory. Resolve the static dir as path.resolve(import.meta.dir, '..', '..', 'web', 'dist'). If the file exists, return new Response(Bun.file(filePath)). If not found and the path does not start with /api, serve index.html for SPA routing. Return 404 for missing static assets.

   websocket object:
   - open(ws): Add ws to clients set. Send init message with all workflows via ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'init', workflows: registry.getAllRuns() })).
   - close(ws): Remove ws from clients set.
   - message(ws, message): Parse string message as JSON. For start_workflow type, call startWorkflow and broadcast workflow_started. For select_workflow, load state from filesystem and send it back to just that client.

5. Define startWorkflow as an inner async function:
   - async function startWorkflow(workflowName: string, taskPrompt: string, maxConcurrent?: number): Promise<string>
   - Call registry.registerRun(workflowName, taskPrompt) to get runId.
   - Broadcast { type: 'workflow_started', summary: the new summary } to all clients.
   - Load workflow via loadWorkflow(workflowName, options.cwd).
   - Determine workDir via getDefaultWorkDir(options.cwd, workflowName).
   - Create web callbacks: const onStatus = createWebCallbacks(runId, broadcast).
   - Start workflow in background without awaiting: workflow.run(taskPrompt, { cwd: options.cwd, workDir, maxConcurrentTasks: maxConcurrent ?? 3, onStatus }).then(() => { registry.completeRun(runId); broadcast complete msg; }).catch((err) => { registry.failRun(runId, ...); broadcast failed msg; }).
   - Return runId.

6. After creating the server, log: Server started at http://host:port.

7. Handle process signals: on SIGINT call server.stop() then process.exit(0).

Make sure the TypeScript compiles with the existing tsconfig. Bun.serve returns a Server object. The websocket config needs message handler, open handler, close handler.

Internal state and refs:

- status: the connection status string
- send: a function (msg: ClientMessage) => void that stringifies and sends via wsRef.current.send if ws is open

Export async function startWebServer(options: WebServerOptions): Promise<void>

Internal state:
- const registry = new RunRegistry()
- const clients = new Set<any>() (Bun ServerWebSocket)
- const WEB_DIST_DIR = join(import.meta.dir, '..', '..', 'web', 'dist')

const broadcast = (msg: ServerMessage) => { const d = JSON.stringify(msg); for (const ws of clients) ws.send(d); }

Use Bun.serve with:

fetch(req, server):
- Parse URL from req.
- If pathname starts with /api/:
  - POST /api/runs: parse JSON body { workflowName, taskPrompt, maxConcurrent? }. Validate fields present. Call internal startWorkflow(). Return Response.json({ runId }).
  - GET /api/runs: Return Response.json(registry.getAllSummaries()).
  - Else: return 404.
- Otherwise serve static from WEB_DIST_DIR:
  - If pathname is '/' or has no extension or file not found: serve index.html.
  - For index.html: read file, replace exact string '{{WS_ENDPOINT}}' with actual ws URL (construct as `ws://${new URL(req.url).host}/ws`). Return with text/html.
  - Other files: lookup MIME type, default application/octet-stream.
  - If index.html doesn't exist either, return 200 with placeholder HTML body explaining frontend not built.

websocket: { open(ws) { clients.add(ws); ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'init', workflows: registry.getAllSummaries() })); }, message(ws, msg) { parse as ClientMessage; handle start_workflow/cancel_workflow/select_workflow }, close(ws) { clients.delete(ws) } }

Internal async function startWorkflow(workflowName, taskPrompt, maxConcurrent?):
1. const runId = registry.createRun(workflowName)
2. broadcast({ type: 'workflow_started', summary: registry.getSummary(runId) })
3. try/catch: const workflow = await loadWorkflow(workflowName, options.cwd). If fails: registry.failRun, broadcast workflow_failed with full summary, return runId.
4. const bridge = createStatusBridge(runId, registry, broadcast)
5. const workDir = getDefaultWorkDir(options.cwd, workflowName)
6. Fire-and-forget: workflow.run(taskPrompt, { cwd: options.cwd, workDir, maxConcurrentTasks: maxConcurrent, onStatus: bridge, signal: registry.getAbortController(runId)!.signal }).then(() => { const summary = registry.completeRun(runId); broadcast({ type: 'workflow_complete', summary }); }).catch((err) => { const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err); const summary = registry.failRun(runId, msg); broadcast({ type: 'workflow_failed', summary, error: msg, phase: registry.getRun(runId)?.currentPhase ?? 'unknown' }); })
7. Return runId.

Note: broadcast of workflow_complete/workflow_failed carries the full updated WorkflowSummary so all clients update their sidebar immediately. The bridge does NOT broadcast workflow_complete/failed — that's the server's job here, avoiding duplicates.

After Bun.serve starts, log the URL. Return the server for testability.

tasks.prompt:
Create web/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts.

Import { useEffect, useRef, useState, useCallback } from 'react'; types from '../types'; isServerMessage from '../types'.

Export function useWebSocket() returning { state: AppGlobalState; send: (msg: ClientMessage) => void; selectRun: (id: string) => void; connected: boolean }.

State: const [state, setState] = useState<AppGlobalState>({ workflows: [], selectedRunId: null, runStates: new Map() })
Refs: wsRef for WebSocket, stateRef synced to latest state.

On mount, determine WS URL: if window.__WS_ENDPOINT__ is set (production), use it; otherwise ws://localhost:3619/ws (dev).

Create WebSocket. On open: log. On close: reconnect after 3 seconds (store timeout in ref, clear on unmount). On error: log.

On message: parse JSON, verify with isServerMessage, update state by message type:
- init: set workflows to message.workflows
- workflow_started: append message.summary to workflows
- workflow_sidebar: update matching workflow's sidebar in workflows array
- workflow_phase: update runState's currentPhase and completedPhases for matching runId
- workflow_complete / workflow_failed: update matching workflow status and completedAt from message.summary
- agent_spawned: add agent to matching run's runState agents Map
- agent_log: append entry to matching agent's log in matching run's runState
- agent_complete: set matching agent's active=false

Important: Create new Map instances for runStates updates (immutable pattern) to trigger React re-renders.

send = useCallback((msg) => wsRef.current?.send(JSON.stringify(msg)), [])
selectRun = useCallback((runId) => { setState(prev => ({...prev, selectedRunId: runId})); send({type:'select_workflow',workflowId:runId}); }, [send])
connected = derived from wsRef readyState === OPEN.

Unmount: close WS, clear reconnect timeout.

Verification: Compiles without errors. cd web && bunx tsc --noEmit passes.

tasks.prompt:
Create web/src/renderers/develop/types.ts.

Import { LogEntry, WorkflowRunState } from '../../types'.

Export:
1. DevelopPhaseInfo = { id: string; label: string; icon: string; status: 'completed'|'active'|'pending' }

- currentPhase: from runState.currentPhase.

Verification: cd web && bunx tsc --noEmit passes.

tasks.prompt:
Create AgentLog.tsx and .css in web/src/renderers/develop/. Replace the placeholder from T16.

Props: { entries: LogEntry[] }

Use @tanstack/react-virtual (useVirtualizer) for virtualized rendering.

Implementation:
1. parentRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
2. isNearBottom ref, updated on scroll: true if scrollTop + clientHeight >= scrollHeight - 100
3. virtualizer = useVirtualizer({ count: entries.length, getScrollElement: () => parentRef.current, estimateSize: (idx) => estimateEntryHeight(entries[idx]), overscan: 5 })
4. estimateEntryHeight: text=60, thinking=40, tool_call_start/end=24, decision=32, error=32, default=24
5. Auto-scroll: useEffect when entries.length changes — if isNearBottom, call virtualizer.scrollToIndex(entries.length-1, {align:'end'})
6. Render: outer div (ref=parentRef, height=100%, overflow-y:auto). Inner div (height=virtualizer.getTotalSize()px, position:relative). Each virtual item: absolute positioned with transform translateY, data-index for measurement.

Entry rendering by type: text→white; thinking→🧠 prefix, secondary color, italic; tool_call_start→🔧 prefix, accent color; tool_call_end→✅/❌ based on isError metadata; tool_call→🔧 prefix; decision→🤝 prefix, warning color; error→⚠️ prefix, error color, bold.

Known edge cases (documented in comments): variable-height content may cause scroll jumps if estimates are far off; rapid updates are batched by React; auto-scroll only triggers when user is near bottom to avoid interrupting manual scroll.

AgentLog.css: .agent-log { height: 100%; overflow-y: auto; font-family: var(--engin-font-mono); font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6; } .log-entry { padding: 2px var(--engin-space-sm); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--engin-bg-surface); }

Verification: cd web && bunx tsc --noEmit passes.

output.strategy: The implementation spans five layers built in dependency order: (1) Backend foundation — widen phase types to string in StatusCallbacks (Option A from feedback), add onSidebarUpdate callback, define WebSocket protocol types, create RunRegistry and StatusBridge. (2) Bun.serve server — HTTP static file serving with {{WS_ENDPOINT}} placeholder replacement (not regex injection), WebSocket lifecycle, fire-and-forget workflow execution with explicit .then/.catch handlers that broadcast full WorkflowSummary on completion/failure. (3) CLI integration — 'web' command with validated --host/--port flags (port validated as integer 1-65535). (4) Frontend — Vite+React pipeline, dark-mode CSS variables, useWebSocket hook managing immutable Map state, Header/Sidebar/layout components, develop workflow renderer with ProgressIndicator + CSS Grid auto-fill AgentGrid + virtualized AgentLog via @tanstack/react-virtual. (5) Develop workflow main.ts — uses StatusCallbacks directly (NOT WorkflowStatusTracker which has incompatible fixed PHASE_ORDER), initialization phase calls pi for title generation, stubs remaining phases. Key decisions addressing feedback: phase types widened to string; workflow_complete/failed messages carry full summary for immediate sidebar updates; develop workflow bypasses WorkflowStatusTracker entirely; port validation mirrors --max-concurrent pattern; index.html uses placeholder string replacement instead of regex injection.

reasoning: The plan is detailed and covers most requirements, but has two critical issues that must be resolved before implementation can proceed. The most severe issues are (1) T20 attempts to import TypeScript-only interfaces (WorkflowModule, WorkflowRunOptions) as runtime values, which will crash at module load time, and (2) T18 imports from T19 (DevelopRenderer) but T19 is neither a dependency of T18 nor does T18's file list include the placeholder it mentions. Additionally, the CSS Grid row-stretching requirement is not correctly implemented, and the virtualizer auto-scroll approach needs improvement. See suggestions below for fixes.

profile.systemPrompt:
You are a general-purpose implementation agent. You execute atomic, well-defined tasks from a plan where all decisions are already made. Follow these rules:

1. **ATOMICITY**: If your task is too large or not atomic — multiple independent features, multiple modules, or requiring architectural decisions — HALT and request the calling agent to split it.

2. **COMPLETE IMPLEMENTATION**: Every requirement must be implemented. No TODOs, placeholders, stub functions, or "implement later" comments. If unclear, HALT and ask.

3. **CODE QUALITY**: Follow existing project patterns exactly — naming, imports, error handling, file organization, shared utilities. New code must be indistinguishable from existing code.

- **summary**: What was implemented
- **verification_status**: Results of compilation and test runs

topics.topic: Overall project structure and requirements coverage

output.overallAssessment: The codebase is well-structured and demonstrates thoughtful architecture. Core functionality (profile loading, harness creation, workflow loading, task tracking, audit logging) is solid with good test coverage (435 core tests pass). The web backend (src/web/) is cleanly implemented with proper WebSocket protocols and run registry. The develop workflow is a functioning example. However, several issues need attention: (1) The test runner configuration doesn't isolate web frontend tests from core tests, causing 194 pre-existing failures when running `bun test` from root. (2) A few test isolation bugs cause flaky failures in workflow and server tests when the full suite runs together. (3) Orphaned build artifacts exist in dist/. (4) Unresolved TODO and unused parameter suggest incomplete work. (5) The `.gitignore` is incomplete for runtime state files. Overall quality is good but needs cleanup before release.

issues.description: Orphaned build artifact: dist/core/tool-registry.* files exist but no corresponding source file in src/core/. These are stale leftovers from a previous build that was removed from source. They are not referenced by any source file and should be cleaned up. While dist/ is gitignored, they could still cause confusion and would be included in any published npm package (package.json's 'files' field includes 'dist').

Unresolved TODO at line 93: '// TODO: Pass actual token counts from the session instead of hardcoding zeros'. The `retryAgentUntil` function sets `totalTokens: { input: 0, output: 0 }` as a placeholder. This is a known limitation that should be tracked as an issue.

Unused parameter `_errorMsg` in `failRun(runId, _errorMsg)` at line 78. The error message is accepted but never stored or used. The underscore prefix suppresses the lint warning, but the parameter should either be used (e.g., stored in the run entry for diagnostics) or removed from the signature entirely to avoid confusion.

Test script (`bun test`) picks up all `*.test.ts` files including web frontend tests in `web/src/`. These React component tests require a jsdom environment (via vitest) and fail with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` when run with bun's built-in test runner. 194 tests fail as a result. The test script should either (a) exclude web tests via a glob pattern, (b) configure bun's test environment per-directory, or (c) add a separate `test:web` script using vitest from the web directory.

Two tests fail due to hardcoded asset filenames: tests for serving `.js` assets (expects `index-DyyqoESW.js`) and `.js.map` assets (expects `index-DyyqoESW.js.map`) fail because the actual built files have different hashes (`index-yrW-nzKR.js`). The tests should dynamically discover the actual asset filenames from the filesystem instead of hardcoding them.

Test isolation issue: develop workflow tests pass when run in isolation but fail when run together with other test files (particularly web/server.test.ts). The mock setup uses `mock.module('@harms-haus/engin')` with an `afterAll` restore that may not properly isolate mocks when other test suites also interact with the same module. The `afterAll` hook at line 52 does restore the module, but Bun's mock system may not cleanly separate module-level mocks across files.

Test files in `tests/web/server.test.ts` reference a shared setup that causes cascading failures. The test at line 963 has an issue with `onStatus` being cast as `Record<string, Function>` which loses type safety. When the full suite runs, this test's setup can corrupt the state for subsequent `develop.test.ts` tests.

The `.gitignore` file only covers `.engin/.env` and `.engin-state.json` but not the broader `.engin/work/` directory tree. Runtime state files like `.engin/work/develop/.engin-state.json` could accidentally be committed. Recommendation: add `.engin/work/` or just `.engin/` to `.gitignore` since the entire `.engin/` directory is developer-local configuration.

The `install-global.sh` script is present but not referenced in any documentation (README.md or docs/README.md). It's also not listed as a script in package.json. Users won't discover it exists. Either document it or integrate it as an npm script.

The documentation's CLI reference section does not document the `web` command or the `--host`/`--port` flags that were added. The docs also don't mention the `install-global.sh` script or the web frontend build process.

output.overallAssessment: The codebase is well-structured with clear separation of concerns between core engine, task tracking, pooling, web interface, and CLI. The core abstractions (AgentProfile, Task, WorkflowState, AuditEvent, StatusCallbacks) are thoughtfully designed with good type safety. The lane-pool implementation provides a robust concurrent task processing model with proper error handling, retry logic, and lifecycle callbacks. Test coverage is extensive for backend modules with 555+ passing tests covering most paths. However, there are several issues: missing test coverage for `utils.ts`, a test fragility from hardcoded hashed asset filenames in server tests, mock module leakage causing cross-file test interference in full suite runs, web frontend vitest tests being incorrectly discovered by `bun test`, leftover session data in the `.engin/` directory, and unnecessary artificial delays in the develop workflow.

issues.description: Missing test file. The source file `src/core/utils.ts` exports critical functions (`validateWorkflowName`, `isEnoentError`, `safeErrorMessage`, `DEFAULT_TOOLS`) that have zero unit test coverage.

Tests reference a hardcoded hashed asset filename `/assets/index-DyyqoESW.js` which does not match the actual built file `/assets/index-yrW-nzKR.js` in `web/dist/assets/`. This causes 2 test failures every time the frontend is rebuilt with different hash values. The asset filename should be resolved dynamically or the test should verify content type generically without relying on a specific filename.

These vitest-based frontend tests (in `web/src/**/__tests__/*.test.tsx`) are discovered by `bun test` from the project root but cannot execute correctly because they require jsdom, React Testing Library, and vitest-specific configuration. This causes 172+ test failures in full suite runs. These test files should be excluded from `bun test` discovery, either via a test file naming convention, a `test.exclude` config in `bunfig.toml`, or by running frontend tests only via the `test:web` script.

The develop workflow's `remainingPhases` loop introduces an unnecessary 50ms `setTimeout` delay per phase (8 × 50ms = 400ms+). This artificial delay serves no functional purpose and slows down workflow execution, particularly in test environments where it adds over 300ms per test case.

The `.engin/work/develop/` directory contains a large number of session files (~100+ JSONL files) from previous workflow runs. This leftover session data is not gitignored (only `.engin-state.json` is in `.gitignore`) and may affect disk usage or test behavior. Consider cleaning session data or adding appropriate gitignore patterns.

The `retryAgentUntil` function hardcodes `totalTokens` as `{ input: 0, output: 0 }` with a TODO comment indicating actual token counts should be passed from the session. This means token tracking for structured output retries is lost.

In `LanePool.run()`, `failedTasks` is calculated as `allTasks.length - completedTasks`. This assumes every non-completed task is a failure, which is misleading when the pool is cancelled mid-execution (via AbortSignal) — tasks still in 'claimed' or 'implementing' state are incorrectly counted as failed rather than cancelled.

output.overallAssessment: The codebase implements a comprehensive multi-agent workflow engine with a new web UI server. The core library, pool/lane system, and tracking modules are well-structured with thorough test coverage. However, there are three critical issues: (1) the TypeScript build is broken due to a missing generic type parameter on `Bun.Server` in the new web server module, (2) test isolation is broken because `server.test.ts` leaks module-level mocks via top-level `mock.module()` calls without cleanup, causing 18 downstream test failures when all tests run together, and (3) numerous ESLint violations across new and existing files, including unused imports, non-null assertions, and empty-function stubs. Additionally, there is a pre-existing TODO for token tracking that remains unresolved. The web frontend tests all pass, and all individual backend test suites pass in isolation, confirming the core logic is sound.

issues.description: TypeScript build failure: `Bun.Server` requires a generic type parameter (`Bun.Server<WebSocketData>`). Change line 9 from `Promise<Bun.Server>` to `Promise<Bun.Server<undefined>>` to fix. This prevents `tsc` from completing, blocking all downstream build steps.

Module-level `mock.module('../../src/core/workflow-loader.ts', ...)` and `mock.module('../../src/core/config.ts', ...)` are called at the top of the file without any `afterAll` restoration. These mocks persist across test files in the same Bun process, contaminating `tests/workflows/develop.test.ts` (which loads the actual develop workflow module that imports from workflow-loader). This causes 18 failing tests when running the full suite (`bun test tests/`), even though each test file passes in isolation.
Unused import `RunRegistry` on line 5. Remove the import or prefix with underscore to satisfy the ESLint `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` rule.
Unused binding `started` on line 548 (assigned but never read). Either use it or remove the assignment to satisfy `prefer-const` and unused-vars rules.
`abortPromiseResolve` on line 575 is assigned but never reassigned; should use `const` instead of `let`.
Unused import `WorkflowSummary` on line 3. Remove it or prefix with underscore.
ESLint: `clients` is typed as `Set<any>` (line 11). Use a concrete type or `Set<Bun.ServerWebSocket<unknown>>` to avoid the `no-explicit-any` violation.
ESLint: Forbidden non-null assertion on `registry.getRun(runId)!` (line 57) and `registry.getAbortController(runId)!` (line 118 in the catch handler). Use a conditional check instead.
ESLint: `filePath` (line 118) is never reassigned; use `const` instead of `let`.
ESLint: Empty arrow function `.catch(() => {})` on line 189 triggers `no-empty-function`. Use a no-op sentinel or remove the catch if error is intentionally swallowed.

ESLint: Multiple empty method stubs (`onWorkflowStart`, `onWorkflowComplete`, etc., lines 18-24) trigger `no-empty-function`. These are necessary as no-op callbacks but should be explicitly allowed via an ESLint comment or disabled for the file.
ESLint: Import `TurnContentBlock` on line 3 should use `import type` since it is used only as a type.
ESLint: Forbidden non-null assertions at lines 34, 43, 167. Use optional chaining or conditional checks instead of `!.`
ESLint: Constructor-style generic `Map<string, RunEntry>` on line 34 triggers `consistent-generic-constructors`. Use `new Map<string, RunEntry>()` or `new Map()` with type annotation.
ESLint: Forbidden non-null assertion on `this.runs.get(id)!` at line 196.
ESLint: Line 99 uses `Array<{ id: string; label: string; icon: string }>` which triggers `array-type`. Use `{ id: string; label: string; icon: string }[]` instead.

Pre-existing TODO at line 93: `// TODO: Pass actual token counts from the session instead of hardcoding zeros`. Token tracking remains incomplete — `retryAgentUntil` always returns zero tokens despite the harness subscribe logic being able to extract usage. This is a known gap that should be addressed in a follow-up.

The `startWorkflow` function catches `loadWorkflow` errors and broadcasts `workflow_failed`, but the same error-handling pattern is duplicated in the `.catch()` of the `workflow.run().then().catch()` chain. The `registry.failRun` and broadcast logic is duplicated — extracting a shared failure handler would reduce duplication risk.
